exams.name: United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE)
exams.notes: Applicant must pass steps or levels one, two, and three within three attempts each; step or level three must be passed within five years of passing step or level two, or before the end of residency training.
exams.quote: The applicant taking the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) or Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination (COMLEX-USA) must have passed steps or levels one, two, and three. The applicant must pass each of steps or levels one, two, and three with passing scores as recommended by the USMLE program or National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners within three attempts.

exams.name: Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination (COMLEX-USA)
exams.notes: Alternative to USMLE for osteopathic applicants; same three-attempt rule applies.
exams.jurisdiction: national (National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners)
exams.quote: The applicant taking the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) or Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination (COMLEX-USA) must have passed steps or levels one, two, and three.

exams.name: Special Purpose Examination (SPEX) of the Federation of State Medical Boards
exams.notes: Required only if the primary examination was passed more than ten years ago and the applicant does not have current specialty board certification.
exams.quote: pass the special purpose examination of the Federation of State Medical Boards with a score of 75 or better within three attempts

required.quote: The licensee must meet the continuing education requirements under Minnesota Rules, chapter 5605.

requirements.value: Applicant must have passed an approved examination, hold a current license from equivalent licensing agency in another state or Canada, and meet good moral character, education, and training requirements. If examination was passed more than ten years ago, must pass SPEX within three attempts or have current specialty board certification.
requirements.quote: The applicant shall satisfy all the requirements established in section 147.02, subdivision 1, paragraphs (a), (b), (d), (e), and (f), or section 147.037, subdivision 1, paragraphs (a) to (e).

title_protection.quote: A person not licensed under this chapter is prohibited from using the title "doctor of medicine," "medical doctor," "doctor of osteopathic medicine," "osteopathic physician," "physician," "surgeon," "M.D.," or "D.O." in the conduct of any occupation or profession pertaining to the diagnosis of human disease or conditions.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to demonstrate the qualifications or satisfy the requirements for a license.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to demonstrate the qualifications or satisfy the requirements for a license contained in this chapter or rules of the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Obtaining a license by fraud, cheating, or attempting to subvert the licensing examination process.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Obtaining a license by fraud or cheating, or attempting to subvert the licensing examination process.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction within the previous five years of a felony reasonably related to the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction, during the previous five years, of a felony reasonably related to the practice of medicine or osteopathic medicine.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Revocation, suspension, restriction, or other disciplinary action against the person's medical license in another state or jurisdiction.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Revocation, suspension, restriction, limitation, or other disciplinary action against the person's medical license in another state or jurisdiction, failure to report to the board that charges regarding the person's license have been brought in another state or jurisdiction, or having been refused a license by any other state or jurisdiction.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising which is false or misleading, violates board rules, or claims without substantiation the positive cure of any disease.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Advertising which is false or misleading, which violates any rule of the board, or which claims without substantiation the positive cure of any disease, or professional superiority to or greater skill than that possessed by another physician.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating a rule promulgated by the board or an order of the board, or a state or federal law relating to the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating a rule promulgated by the board or an order of the board, a state, or federal law which relates to the practice of medicine, or in part regulates the practice of medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in unethical or improper conduct, including conduct likely to deceive or harm the public, or professionally incompetent medical practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in any unethical or improper conduct, including but not limited to: (1) conduct likely to deceive or defraud the public; (2) conduct likely to harm the public; (3) conduct that demonstrates a willful or careless disregard for the health, welfare, or safety of a patient; (4) medical practice that is professionally incompetent

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide proper supervision of a licensed or unlicensed health care provider or a physician under any agreement with the board.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to provide proper supervision, including but not limited to supervision of a: (1) licensed or unlicensed health care provider; and (2) physician under any agreement with the board.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding or abetting an unlicensed person in the practice of medicine.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Aiding or abetting an unlicensed person in the practice of medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Adjudication by a court as mentally incompetent, mentally ill, developmentally disabled, chemically dependent, or dangerous to the public.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Adjudication by a court of competent jurisdiction, within or outside this state, as: (1) mentally incompetent; (2) mentally ill; (3) developmentally disabled; (4) a chemically dependent person; (5) a person dangerous to the public

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conduct that departs from or fails to conform to the minimal standards of acceptable and prevailing medical practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conduct that departs from or fails to conform to the minimal standards of acceptable and prevailing medical practice in which case proof of actual injury need not be established.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Inability to practice medicine with reasonable skill and safety by reason of illness, intoxication, drug use, mental or physical condition, or diminished capacity.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Inability to practice medicine with reasonable skill and safety to patients by reason of the following, including but not limited to: (1) illness; (2) intoxication; (3) use of drugs, narcotics, chemicals, or any other type of substance; (4) mental condition; (5) physical condition; (6) diminished cognitive ability; (7) loss of motor skills; or (8) deterioration through the aging process.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Revealing a privileged communication from or relating to a patient except when otherwise required or permitted by law.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Revealing a privileged communication from or relating to a patient except when otherwise required or permitted by law.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure by a doctor of osteopathic medicine to identify the school of healing in professional use of the doctor's name.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure by a doctor of osteopathic medicine to identify the school of healing in the professional use of the doctor's name by one of the following terms: osteopathic physician and surgeon, doctor of osteopathic medicine, or D.O.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Improper management of medical records, including failure to maintain adequate records or comply with patient requests.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Improper management of medical records, including failure to maintain adequate medical records, to comply with a patient's request made pursuant to sections 144.291 to 144.298, or to furnish a medical record or report required by law.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Fee splitting, including paying or receiving commissions for referrals, dividing fees improperly, or referring patients for self-benefit without disclosure.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Fee splitting, including without limitation: (1) paying, offering to pay, receiving, or agreeing to receive, a commission, rebate, or remuneration, directly or indirectly, primarily for the referral of patients or the prescription of drugs or devices

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in abusive or fraudulent billing practices, including violations of federal Medicare and Medicaid laws or state medical assistance laws.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in abusive or fraudulent billing practices, including violations of the federal Medicare and Medicaid laws or state medical assistance laws.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Becoming addicted or habituated to a drug or intoxicant.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Becoming addicted or habituated to a drug or intoxicant.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Inappropriate prescribing of or failure to properly prescribe a drug or device.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Inappropriate prescribing of or failure to properly prescribe a drug or device, including prescribing a drug or device for other than medically accepted therapeutic or experimental or investigative purposes authorized by a state or federal agency.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in conduct with a patient which is sexual or may reasonably be interpreted as sexual.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in conduct with a patient which is sexual or may reasonably be interpreted by the patient as sexual, or in any verbal behavior which is seductive or sexually demeaning to a patient.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to make required reports or to cooperate with a board investigation.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to make reports as required by section 147.111 or to cooperate with an investigation of the board as required by section 147.131.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly providing false or misleading information directly related to the care of a patient.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Knowingly providing false or misleading information that is directly related to the care of that patient unless done for an accepted therapeutic purpose such as the administration of a placebo.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding suicide or aiding attempted suicide in violation of Minnesota law.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Aiding suicide or aiding attempted suicide in violation of section 609.215

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practice of a board-regulated profession under lapsed or nonrenewed credentials.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practice of a board-regulated profession under lapsed or nonrenewed credentials.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to repay a state or federally secured student loan in accordance with the provisions of the loan.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to repay a state or federally secured student loan in accordance with the provisions of the loan.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Providing interstate telehealth services other than according to the applicable statutory provision.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Providing interstate telehealth services other than according to section 147.032.

definition_quote.value: a person not exempted under section 147.09 is 'practicing medicine' or engaged in the 'practice of medicine' if the person does any of the following: (1) advertises, holds out to the public, or represents in any manner that the person is authorized to practice medicine in this state; (2) offers or undertakes to prescribe, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another; (3) offers or undertakes to prevent or to diagnose, correct, or treat in any manner or by any means, methods, devices, or instrumentalities, any disease, illness, pain, wound, fracture, infirmity, deformity or defect of any person; (4) offers or undertakes to perform any surgical operation including any invasive or noninvasive procedures involving the use of a laser or laser assisted device, upon any person; or (5) offers to undertake to use hypnosis for the treatment or relief of any wound, fracture, or bodily injury, infirmity, or disease.
definition_quote.quote: a person not exempted under section 147.09 is "practicing medicine" or engaged in the "practice of medicine" if the person does any of the following: (1) advertises, holds out to the public, or represents in any manner that the person is authorized to practice medicine in this state; (2) offers or undertakes to prescribe, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another; (3) offers or undertakes to prevent or to diagnose, correct, or treat in any manner or by any means, methods, devices, or instrumentalities, any disease, illness, pain, wound, fracture, infirmity, deformity or defect of any person; (4) offers or undertakes to perform any surgical operation including any invasive or noninvasive procedures involving the use of a laser or laser assisted device, upon any person; or (5) offers to undertake to use hypnosis for the treatment or relief of any wound, fracture, or bodily injury, infirmity, or disease.

drug_authority.quote: offers or undertakes to prescribe, give, or administer any drug or medicine for the use of another

license_status_types.quote: The board may charge the following nonrefundable application and license fees processed pursuant to sections 147.02, 147.03, 147.037, 147.0375, and 147.38: (1) physician application fee, $200; (2) physician annual registration renewal fee, $192; ... (4) physician emeritus license, $50; (6) nonrenewable 24-month limited license, $392

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical school graduates must: present evidence of graduation from a board-approved school equivalent to accredited US/Canadian schools; have been awarded an ECFMG certificate and have working English ability; complete one year of accredited graduate clinical medical training (with exceptions); pass FSMB or USMLE examinations; and meet all other standard licensure requirements.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: The applicant shall present evidence satisfactory to the board that the applicant has been awarded a certificate by the Educational Council for Foreign Medical Graduates, and the applicant has a working ability in the English language sufficient to communicate with patients and physicians and to engage in the practice of medicine.

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: The applicant shall present evidence satisfactory to the board of the completion of one year of graduate, clinical medical training in a program accredited by a national accrediting organization approved by the board.

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: A physician providing health care services by telehealth in this state shall be held to the same standards of practice and conduct as provided in this chapter for in-person health care services. A physician-patient relationship may be established through telehealth.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: A physician providing health care services by telehealth in this state shall be held to the same standards of practice and conduct as provided in this chapter for in-person health care services.

telemedicine_license_available.quote: A physician not licensed to practice medicine in this state may provide medical services to a patient located in this state through interstate telehealth if the following conditions are met: ... interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: The Interstate Medical Licensure Compact is enacted into law and entered into with all other jurisdictions legally joining in it

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: Four times each year as prescribed by the board, each insurer authorized to sell insurance described in section 60A.06, subdivision 1, clause (13), and providing professional liability insurance to persons regulated by the board, shall submit to the board a report concerning the regulated persons against whom professional malpractice settlements or awards have been made to the plaintiff.

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Any hospital, clinic, prepaid medical plan, or other health care institution or organization located in this state shall report to the board any action taken by the institution or organization or any of its administrators or medical or other committees to revoke, suspend, restrict, or condition a physician's privilege to practice or treat patients in the institution

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: A person licensed under this chapter who is unable to practice with reasonable skill and safety by reason of illness; use of alcohol, drugs, chemicals, or any other materials; or as a result of a mental, physical, or psychological condition may participate in the health professional services program under sections 214.31 to 214.36 if the person meets the eligibility requirements.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: If the board has probable cause to believe that a regulated person comes under subdivision 1, paragraph (1), it may direct the person to submit to a mental or physical examination.

locum_tenens_permit_available.quote: An applicant for licensure under this section may request the board to issue a temporary permit in accordance with this subdivision. Upon receipt of the application for licensure, a request for a temporary permit, and a nonrefundable physician application fee specified under section 147.01, subdivision 7, the board may issue a temporary permit to practice medicine as a physician if the applicant is: (1) currently licensed in good standing to practice medicine as a physician in another state, territory, or Canadian province
